subject: Post-call: admin & API activity logs — questions and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hall <claire.hall@trucarehealth.com>, Matt Durand <matt.durand@trucarehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: admin & API activity logs — questions and next steps

Hi Claire & Matt,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and a short list of follow-ups so your security team can evaluate the audit/logging surface for SOC 2 and HIPAA review.

Summary of what we covered:
- Admin activity: UI-driven changes (role grants, policy changes), service account usage, and IAM events.
- API logs: full request/response metadata (headers, path, authenticated principal), latency and status codes.
- Exportability: on-demand exports in NDJSON, filtered by tenant, time range, or actor; live streaming to customer-owned S3/GCS.
- Immutability options: write-once S3 lifecycle + signed event hashes for tamper-evidence.

Open questions we promised to clarify (we'll follow up in detail):
1) Retention windows you require for logs and whether immutability for a specific retention period is needed.
2) Format & delivery: do you need event-level JSON (NDJSON) or aggregated CSV summaries for auditors?
3) Auditor access model: do you prefer a read-only export bundle vs. temporary viewer role into a sandbox?

Action items / Next steps:
- I attached a short draft export spec (redwood-admin-log-export-spec-ndjson-v1.pdf) showing fields, sample event, and hashing approach.
- We can run a 30–45 minute technical walkthrough with your security engineer next week to demo an export and show immutability artifacts. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.
- Please fill the attached vendor questionnaire draft where helpful; we can pre-populate answers for standard items.

If you want, we can also prepare a one-off evidence bundle (7–14 day sample) for your auditor that includes: raw NDJSON export, signed hash manifest, and a short README describing verification steps.

Thanks — I’ll let Rachel/Connor chime in on the technical timeline.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-admin-log-export-spec-ndjson-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Claire Hall <claire.hall@trucarehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Durand <matt.durand@trucarehealth.com>, security@trucarehealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: admin & API activity logs — questions and next steps

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our security team after reading the spec: 

1) Retention: For SOC 2 and our internal policy we need 7 years of admin activity and 1 year of API request-level logs by default. Are there cost/size implications for keeping 7 years in an immutable state?

2) Immutability: The signed-hash approach looks promising. Can you confirm whether the manifest includes per-event signatures or a per-batch Merkle root? Our auditors prefer per-event verification if feasible.

3) Export verification: Will Redwood provide a verification utility (open-source script) to validate the signed hashes against the NDJSON bundle?

4) Pseudonymization: For HIPAA we may need certain fields redacted or tokenized in delivered exports. Can exports be filtered to redact PHI fields while preserving event integrity?

We'd like the 30–45 minute demo; Tue 11/17 at 10am PT works for our security engineer.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Hall
Director, Information Security | TruCare Health
claire.hall@trucarehealth.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: admin & API activity logs — questions and next steps

Hi Claire — Rachel here (security & compliance lead on the account). Quick answers below, plus a couple of items we'll bring to the demo: 

Answers: 
- Retention/cost: We support multiple tiers. Immutable storage can be configured as write-once object storage backed to S3 with retention policy; cost depends on the storage class you choose. For 7 years we typically recommend using Glacier Deep Archive (we can provide calculators).
- Immutability model: We produce both per-event signed HMACs and an optional batch Merkle root for efficient verification. Per-event signatures are available and included in the NDJSON event envelope (field: event_signature).
- Verification tooling: Yes — we will attach an open-source verification script (Python) you can run offline against the NDJSON + manifest. We can also provide a short runbook for your auditor.
- Pseudonymization: Exports support field-level redaction/tokenization rules. If you need a pre-redacted evidence bundle for the auditor, we can generate it and still provide signatures over the redacted payload (signature covers redacted output).

What we'll demo on 11/17 (10am PT):
- Live NDJSON export of a 7-day sample for a test tenant (with per-event signatures)
- Verification demo using the script (showing signature checks and manifest)
- Options to stream to your S3 vs. one-off export bundle generation

Action items for TruCare before the call:
- Confirm whether auditor needs per-event raw payloads or redacted copies (reply to this thread)
- If you can, fill the questionnaire draft so we can pre-populate the answers and save time.

Connor and I will prepare the sample export and the verification script. See attached draft questionnaire for any missing items.

Cheers,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
